newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle trade at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle trade at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Wednesday were quiet, with packers and cattle owners locked in a stalemate, feedlot sources said.
Packer buyers continued to bid $66.00 per cwt amid light to moderate interest, but the bids were passed by owners who maintained cattle pricing at $68.00 to $69.00, they said.

Owners clung to firm price attitudes amid ideas beef demand will improve after the upcoming Easter weekend. Some trade sources believe that after U.S. consumers have had their fill of traditional Easter fare such as lamb and ham, they will have a taste for beef.
Cattle feeders' pricing stance also was tied to smaller numbers of fed cattle on showlists this week than last week, some sources said.
